A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAFLe and provide readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting a reliable comparison. All nine pages of v1 and ten pages of v2 were inspected; neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original SAFLe accuracy, communication, runtime, and ablation results on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original SAFLe benchmark and ablation results and adds results on ISIC 2019 under label noise.

M1.justification: Sections 3.1–3.3 retain the same bucketing, fixed shuffling and grouping, embedding summation, least-squares objective, and single-round aggregation procedure. The added evaluations introduce no method component or adaptation.

E1.justification: v2 adds ISIC 2019 skin-lesion classification with corrupted labels, extending evaluation from natural-image benchmarks to medical imaging and a distinct label-noise scenario. CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and Tiny-ImageNet remain covered.

E2.justification: Section 4.2 adds numerical comparisons with TOFA on CIFAR-10/100 and with FedNoRo and FedCorr+LA on noisy ISIC 2019, substantially broadening comparison to pretrained one-shot and specialized noise-robust methods. Existing comparator memberships in Tables 1 and 3 remain unchanged. Newly discussed WiSARD, FedSD2C, and FedCGS are not experimentally compared.

E3.justification: v2 adds evaluation at label-noise rates 0.2, 0.3, 0.4, and 0.6, while omitting v1's matched-accuracy runtime comparison across DeepAFL depths. Retained benchmarks keep their partition settings, default client count, backbones, and metrics. The new noise-generation and comparison protocols are insufficiently detailed to establish fully matched conditions.

E4.justification: v2 adds a distinct robustness investigation testing label corruption without explicit noise correction, using four ISIC 2019 noise levels and specialized comparators. It removes the model-size/capacity fairness analysis. Existing bucketing, embedding-sparsity, backbone, and client-count analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 1 retains averages and standard deviations after unspecified multiple runs, and Table 2 retains its uncertainty reporting. Neither version specifies additional run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. New comparisons use point estimates, a practice already present in Table 3.

E6.justification: v2 adds ISIC 2019 SAFLe results of 69.47%, 67.82%, 66.53%, and 62.94%, together with quoted FedNoRo and FedCorr+LA scores. It adds TOFA scores of 93.18%/76.63% alongside previously reported SAFLe scores of 95.31%/77.83%. It removes runtime results of 114/128/143 seconds for SAFLe versus 130.7/145.7/190.0 seconds for DeepAFL, plus model-size results. Tables 1–3 and Figures 2–6 retain their values; the additions do not establish performance improvements over v1 under matched settings.

T1.justification: Lemma 1, Theorem 1, and Equations 1–18 retain the same definitions, objectives, derivations, and proofs. Differences are citation numbering and pagination.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets, and conclusion retain the same claims about nonlinear expressivity, linear equivalence, single-round aggregation, heterogeneity invariance, and superiority over AFL and DeepAFL. The central contribution scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 adds the interpretation that SAFLe's analytic formulation provides intrinsic label-noise robustness without specialized correction. It removes v1's argument that extra parameters cannot explain the accuracy gains and its measured computational-speed advantage. Existing bucketing and sparsity explanations remain substantively intact.

D1.justification: v2 removes the RTX 4090 hardware disclosure, detailed training times, and the disclosure of embedding size below 0.3 MB relative to an approximately 44 MB backbone. This reduces resource and reproducibility information without establishing an actual hardware or implementation change.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 expands positioning around personalization, architectural adaptation, FedSD2C, and FedCGS; new Section 2.4 distinguishes analytic learning from federated WiSARD aggregation. TOFA and noise-robust learning references are added, while FedCVAE-Ens, FedGen, and FedDisco discussions and references disappear. DeepAFL's updated authorship and venue describe the same work.

P1.justification: v2 locally rewrites the federated-learning background and ablation discussions, adds Section 2.4 and new comparison paragraphs, and removes the model-size and runtime paragraphs. It also corrects wording, the CIFAR-1.0 typo, and author affiliations. The overall section sequence and most methodological prose remain intact.

P2.justification: All six figure graphics and all three tables retain their content and captions. Figure 3 moves from page 6 to page 7, other figures and Table 3 shift position, and text reflows around them. No figure or table is added or redesigned.

improvement.justification: v2 broadens research positioning and adds medical-image robustness evidence, but removes explicit model-size, runtime, and hardware information supporting the paper's efficiency claims. The new TOFA and ISIC comparisons lack sufficient protocol detail to establish fully comparable conditions. These benefits and losses leave the net effect on overall quality unclear.
